title: RustFS
name: rustfs
description: S3-compatible object storage written in Rust, an open-source alternative to MinIO, with a web console for browsing buckets and managing users, policies and access keys. Source: https://github.com/rustfs/rustfs

env.name: RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY
env.label: Admin password (secret key, required)
env.description: Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 16. To change it later, change it here and redeploy.

env.name: RUSTFS_API_PORT
env.label: Host port for the S3 API

env.name: RUSTFS_CONSOLE_PORT
env.label: Host port for the web console

note: Set the secret key before you deploy, since the stack won't start without one. Then open the console at http://<your-host>:9011 (or whichever port you picked) and log in with the admin user as the account (admin unless you changed it) and the secret key as the key. S3 clients and SDKs go to http://<your-host>:9010, with path-style addressing and region us-east-1. Buckets start private. Rather than hand the admin's keys to other apps, make them their own user under Users. Changing the secret key on the form and redeploying changes the admin's password, and other users carry on as they were. Everything lives in the rustfs-data volume, as a single drive with no redundancy, so back it up like any other data. Docs: docs.rustfs.com
